## Objectives

Test and evaluate the closed-loop performance of the USV's speed and yaw-rate controllers in the following scenarios:

| Experiment | Purpose |
|---|---|
| **Base** | Baseline setup with ArduRover default PID gains, no rate limiters, and no feedforward. Reference against which the other two experiments are compared; inspect the default closed-loop behavior in both the speed and yaw-rate channels. |
| **FeedForward** | Add the feedforward gain (using values from our open-loop system identification lab) to both control loops, keeping the PID gains at the Base values. Observe contribution of feedforward to performance. |
| **Tuned** | Tune the PID gains for the "best" response, keeping the feedforward from the previous case. |

: {tbl-colwidths="[15, 85]"}

For each experiment, both the **speed (surge / throttle)** loop and the **yaw-rate (steering / rudder)** loop are exercised with step inputs and the responses logged. Choose either of two optional methods: the pilot applies the step manually with the RC transmitter, or the planner runs a step-input script in Mission Planner. For scripted yaw-rate steps, the pilot holds steady throttle while the script commands steering. See the [procedure](procedure.qmd) for both methods and the required RC input channel checks.

For each of the six cases (three experiments × two channels), you will

* Plot the closed-loop step response timeseries to visualize the transient and steady-state behavior.
* Plot the PID internals (target vs actual, per-term breakdown) to understand how the controller is operating and generating the actuator commands.  This includes the *controller effort* (P/I/D/FF) breakdown, which is critical for understanding the relative contribution of each term to the overall response and diagnosing issues like excessive overshoot (too much P), long settling time (too little D), or integrator windup (excessive I).  Controller effort is also a key aspect of the "best" response characterization, since we want to achieve good performance with minimal control effort.
* Quantify the transient and steady-state performance metrics, then compare across the three experiments for each channel.
  * Review the [example results](results.qmd): timeseries and PID signals for each of the six cases (plus an integrator-windup demonstration) and a summary of performance metrics.

## Schedule

**This week:** clean step-response logs for all **three experiments × two channels = six datasets**, with a brief quality-check.

**Next week:** isolate one step from each log, quantify rise time, settling time, overshoot, and steady-state error, compare across the three experiments, and assemble the slide deck described in the [Deliverable](deliverable.qmd).

## Materials

### For Students

- Shared data repository: [ME2801_USV_Shared](https://nps01-my.sharepoint.com/:f:/g/personal/bbingham_nps_edu/IgBrVQgpC7VsQ4pnhatXVfWBAatl-so1kOaAatxqty9Bj7g?e=C0EGzJ).  This is where to upload your raw (`*.BIN`) autopilot logs for processing.  Add a subfolder for your team (e.g. `TeamX`) and upload there.  The instructors will convert the logs to MATLAB (`*.mat`) format.
- **Optional step-input script** — [download `step_input.py`](files/step_input.py){download="step_input.py"}. Runs in Mission Planner's **DATA / Flight Data → Scripts** tab. The speed example starts at **1550 PWM** for **30 seconds**; verify the throttle and steering RC input channels before setting `CHANNEL`. See the [script instructions](procedure.qmd#step-input-script) before running it.
- **Quick-look script** — [`closedloop_quicklook.m`](https://github.com/bsb808/me2801/blob/main/book/w07_lab_usv_pid/code/closedloop_quicklook.m). Checks a `.mat` log for missing channels, prints its UTC start time, and plots the speed, yaw-rate and actuator channels. Use it for the quality check in [Procedure §5](procedure.qmd#post-processing-and-quality-check).
- **Analysis script** — [`closedloop_assess_example.m`](https://github.com/bsb808/me2801/blob/main/book/w07_lab_usv_pid/code/closedloop_assess_example.m). Loads a single `.mat`, isolates one step, plots the timeseries and PID internals, and reports the step-response metrics. See the [Deliverable](deliverable.qmd) for how to run it on each log.
- **Example log** — [`closedloop_assess_example.mat`](https://github.com/bsb808/me2801/blob/main/book/w07_lab_usv_pid/code/closedloop_assess_example.mat). A known-good speed-step log for testing both scripts before you have your own data; put it in the same folder as the scripts.

### For Instructors

Students are welcome to use these, but explaining them is beyond the scope of the class.

- [`closedloop_assess_main.m`](https://github.com/bsb808/me2801/blob/main/book/w07_lab_usv_pid/code/closedloop_assess_main.m) — extension of the same logic as [`closedloop_assess_example.m`](https://github.com/bsb808/me2801/blob/main/book/w07_lab_usv_pid/code/closedloop_assess_example.m) to process the full dataset. 
- Log conversion — [`bin2mat.py`](https://github.com/bsb808/me2801/blob/main/utils/ardu_utils/bin2mat.py)
